The system categorizes people into seasonal types (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter) with sub-types for more precision.
home.faq2Q: How does AI color analysis work?

These measurements are compared against the 12-season color system to find your best match.

faceQuiz.title: Free Face Shape Quiz
faceQuiz.description: Answer 6 quick questions to discover your face shape and get personalized hairstyle recommendations.
faceQuiz.noAccount: No account required · Takes about 1 minute
faceQuiz.seoIntro: Knowing your face shape is the key to choosing flattering hairstyles, glasses, and makeup techniques. Our free quiz analyzes your facial proportions — forehead width, jawline shape, face length-to-width ratio, and cheekbone prominence — to classify you as one of 7 face shapes: oval, round, square, heart, oblong, diamond, or triangle. Professional makeup artists use these same measurements. While AI photo analysis can measure exact proportions, this quiz gives you a reliable result in under 60 seconds with no photo upload needed.
faceQuiz.faq1Q: How many face shapes are there?
faceQuiz.faq1A: There are 7 main face shapes: oval, round, square, heart, oblong (rectangle), diamond, and triangle. Most people are a blend of two shapes, but one type usually dominates. Knowing your primary shape helps you choose the most flattering hairstyles and accessories.
faceQuiz.faq2Q: How do I determine my face shape?
faceQuiz.faq2A: You can determine your face shape by comparing 4 measurements: forehead width, cheekbone width, jawline width, and face length. The easiest method is our quiz, which guides you through these comparisons. For more precision, use our AI face shape analysis that measures your photo directly.
faceQuiz.faq3Q: What is the most common face shape?
faceQuiz.faq3A: Oval and round are the most common face shapes worldwide. Oval faces have balanced proportions and suit most hairstyles. Round faces have similar width and length with soft angles, and look best with styles that add definition.
faceQuiz.faq4Q: Can my face shape change over time?
faceQuiz.faq4A: Yes, face shape can change due to aging, weight fluctuation, and bone structure development. Fat distribution shifts with age, and the jawline may become more defined or softer. It's worth re-checking your face shape every few years.

faceQuiz.result_oval_desc: Considered the most versatile face shape. Your face is slightly longer than wide, with a gently rounded jawline and forehead.
faceQuiz.result_oval_best: Lucky you – almost any hairstyle works! Try layered cuts, bobs, side parts, and both long and short styles.
faceQuiz.result_oval_avoid: Very heavy bangs that hide your balanced proportions.
faceQuiz.result_oval_bangs: Side-swept bangs, curtain bangs, or wispy bangs all work beautifully.
faceQuiz.result_round_desc: Your face has soft angles with similar width and length. Full cheeks and a rounded jawline give a youthful appearance.
faceQuiz.result_round_best: Long layers, side parts, asymmetrical bobs, and styles with height at the crown to elongate your face.
faceQuiz.result_round_avoid: Chin-length bobs, center parts, and very rounded styles that emphasize width.
faceQuiz.result_round_bangs: Side-swept or diagonal bangs. Avoid blunt, straight-across bangs.
faceQuiz.result_square_desc: Strong jawline with a forehead that's roughly the same width. Your face has angular, defined features.
faceQuiz.result_square_best: Soft layers, waves, side-swept styles, and anything that softens the angles. Long bobs and textured cuts work great.
faceQuiz.result_square_avoid: Blunt, one-length cuts and chin-length bobs that emphasize the jawline.
faceQuiz.result_square_bangs: Side-swept bangs or soft, wispy bangs. Avoid blunt straight bangs.
faceQuiz.result_heart_desc: A wider forehead and cheekbones that taper to a narrower, sometimes pointed chin. Often considered very feminine.
faceQuiz.result_heart_best: Chin-length bobs, long side-swept layers, and styles with volume at the jaw level to balance the narrower chin.
faceQuiz.result_heart_avoid: Styles with lots of volume at the crown or forehead, which emphasize the wider top.
faceQuiz.result_heart_bangs: Curtain bangs or side-swept bangs that soften the forehead width.
faceQuiz.result_oblong_desc: Your face is noticeably longer than it is wide, with a similar forehead and jawline width.
faceQuiz.result_oblong_best: Shoulder-length cuts, waves and curls that add width, side parts, and layered styles.
faceQuiz.result_oblong_avoid: Very long straight hair and styles that add height, which make the face appear longer.
faceQuiz.result_oblong_bangs: Full, blunt bangs to visually shorten the face length.
faceQuiz.result_diamond_desc: Narrow forehead and jawline with wide, high cheekbones. Angular and dramatic features.
faceQuiz.result_diamond_best: Chin-length bobs, side-swept styles, and cuts that add width at the forehead and chin level.
faceQuiz.result_diamond_avoid: Styles that are very narrow at the sides or add volume only at the cheekbones.
faceQuiz.result_diamond_bangs: Side-swept bangs or curtain bangs to add width at the forehead.
faceQuiz.result_triangle_desc: A narrower forehead that widens at the jawline and chin area.
faceQuiz.result_triangle_best: Styles with volume at the top – layered crowns, side parts with lift, and chin-length or shorter styles.
faceQuiz.result_triangle_avoid: Styles that add volume at the jaw level, heavy one-length cuts.
faceQuiz.result_triangle_bangs: Full, voluminous bangs or side-swept bangs to balance the narrower forehead.

hairPage.faq1Q: What is AI hair color analysis?
hairPage.faq1A: AI hair color analysis evaluates your skin undertone, depth, and contrast from a selfie to recommend hair colors that complement your natural coloring. It suggests flattering shades, highlights your best tones, and flags colors that may wash you out.
hairPage.faq2Q: How does Belle determine the best hair color for me?
hairPage.faq2A: Our AI analyzes your skin undertone (warm, cool, or neutral), eye color, and natural hair color from your photo. These factors are matched against color theory principles to identify hair shades — from natural browns and blondes to bold fashion colors — that harmonize with your complexion.
hairPage.faq3Q: Can AI hair color analysis help me before visiting a salon?
hairPage.faq3A: Yes — use the report as a reference when discussing options with your colorist. You'll receive specific shade recommendations, colors to avoid, and styling tips so you can confidently choose a hair color that suits your skin tone.
hairPage.faq4Q: What hair colors should I avoid for my skin tone?
hairPage.faq4A: Your report includes a dedicated section on colors to avoid — shades that clash with your undertone or create unflattering contrast. This helps you steer clear of common mistakes like choosing an ashy blonde on warm skin or a brassy tone on cool undertones.
hairPage.faq5A: Your first AI hair color analysis is free with no signup required. Upload a selfie to receive personalized hair color suggestions, undertone analysis, and styling recommendations.
hairPage.seoIntro: Finding the right hair color is one of the highest-impact beauty decisions you can make — and one of the most expensive to get wrong. A salon color correction can cost $200-500+. AI hair color analysis removes the guesswork by evaluating your skin undertone, natural contrast level, and eye color to predict which hair shades will harmonize with your coloring and which will clash. The difference between a flattering warm caramel and an unflattering ashy blonde often comes down to undertone alignment that is invisible to the untrained eye but obvious in photos. Our AI previews multiple hair colors on your actual face, so you can see the result before committing at the salon.

colorGuide.toc5: How to Find Your Color Season
colorGuide.whatIsP1: Color analysis — also called personal color analysis or seasonal color analysis — is a method of identifying which specific colors look most flattering on you based on your natural coloring: skin undertone, eye color, and hair color. When you wear colors that harmonize with your natural coloring, your skin looks healthier, your features stand out, and you appear more vibrant overall.
colorGuide.whatIsP2: The concept originated with Johannes Itten at the Bauhaus school in the 1920s and was popularized by Carole Jackson's 1980 book Color Me Beautiful. The original 4-season system has since evolved into the more precise 12-season system used by professional color analysts today. In 2026, AI-powered color analysis has made this once-exclusive service accessible to everyone — searches for "color analysis" hit an all-time high in March 2026, up 139% year-over-year.
colorGuide.whatIsP3Korea: Color analysis is especially popular in <koreaLink>Korea (퍼스널컬러)</koreaLink> and Japan (パーソナルカラー), where knowing your seasonal color type is a mainstream part of beauty culture.
colorGuide.howWorksDesc: Color analysis evaluates four key dimensions of your natural coloring. These four measurements determine which of the 12 sub-seasons you belong to and, consequently, which colors will look best on you.
colorGuide.dimUndertoneDesc: Whether your skin has warm (golden/peachy) or cool (pink/rosy) undertones. This is the single most important factor — it determines whether you're in a warm season (Spring/Autumn) or cool season (Summer/Winter).
colorGuide.dimDepthDesc: How light or dark your overall coloring is — considering skin, hair, and eyes together. This separates Light seasons (Light Spring/Light Summer) from Deep seasons (Deep Autumn/Deep Winter).
colorGuide.dimChromaDesc: Whether your coloring is muted (soft, dusty, blended) or clear (vivid, bright, saturated). This distinguishes Soft seasons from Bright seasons.
colorGuide.dimContrastDesc: The difference in lightness between your skin, hair, and eyes. High contrast (dark hair + light skin) vs. low contrast (everything similar in depth) affects which specific colors within your season work best.
colorGuide.fourSeasonDesc: The 4-season system is the foundation of color analysis. It divides people into four broad categories based on undertone and depth. While less precise than the 12-season system, it provides a useful starting point for understanding your best color family.
colorGuide.springDesc: Warm undertones with light, clear coloring. Colors are warm, fresh, and lively.
colorGuide.summerDesc: Cool undertones with light-to-medium, muted coloring. Colors are cool, soft, and elegant.
colorGuide.autumnDesc: Warm undertones with medium-to-deep, muted coloring. Colors are warm, rich, and earthy.
colorGuide.winterDesc: Cool undertones with medium-to-deep, clear coloring. Colors are bold, cool, and dramatic.
colorGuide.midCtaTitle: Not sure which season you are?

colorGuide.twelveSeasonDesc: The 12-season system refines each of the four seasons into three sub-types, accounting for variations in depth, chroma, and the "bridge" between adjacent seasons. This system, developed from the Sci\ART method, provides significantly more precise color recommendations.
colorGuide.findSeasonTitle: How to Find Your Color Season
colorGuide.findSeasonDesc: There are three main methods to determine your seasonal color type, each with different trade-offs in accuracy, cost, and convenience.
colorGuide.methodAIDesc: Upload a bare-face selfie in natural light and get your 12-season color type in 60 seconds. AI analyzes your undertone, depth, contrast, and chroma using computer vision — the same color science principles professional colorists use. Free to try, no appointment needed.

colorGuide.methodProDesc: An in-person consultation where a trained colorist holds colored fabric swatches near your face and observes how each color affects your complexion. The gold standard for accuracy, especially for ambiguous or edge cases.

colorGuide.useResultsDesc: Once you know your season, here's how to apply it across every aspect of your appearance.
colorGuide.useMakeupDesc: Choose foundation, blush, lip, and eye colors in your season's palette. Warm seasons (Spring/Autumn) suit peach, coral, and warm berry shades. Cool seasons (Summer/Winter) suit pink, mauve, and cool berry tones.
colorGuide.useWardrobeDesc: Build your capsule wardrobe around your season's best neutrals and accent colors. This eliminates decision fatigue and ensures everything in your closet works together.
colorGuide.useHairDesc: Choose hair colors that complement your season rather than fighting it. Warm seasons suit golden, copper, and auburn tones. Cool seasons suit ash, cool brown, and burgundy tones.
colorGuide.useJewelryDesc: Match metal tones to your undertone — gold, copper, and bronze for warm types; silver, platinum, and white gold for cool types. Gemstone choices follow the same warm/cool logic.

colorGuide.faq1A: Color analysis (also called personal color analysis or seasonal color analysis) is a method of identifying the specific colors that look most flattering on you based on your natural coloring — skin undertone, eye color, and hair color. It uses the 12-season system to categorize people into types like Soft Autumn or Bright Winter, each with its own recommended color palette for makeup, clothing, hair, and accessories.
colorGuide.faq2A: Color analysis evaluates four dimensions of your natural coloring: undertone (warm vs. cool), depth (light vs. dark), chroma (muted vs. clear), and contrast (difference between your lightest and darkest features). These four measurements map to one of 12 sub-seasons, each with its own ideal color palette. Traditional methods use fabric draping; AI methods analyze these dimensions from a photo.
colorGuide.faq3Q: Can I do color analysis at home?
colorGuide.faq3A: Yes. You can start with a free online quiz for a basic estimate, or use AI color analysis for more accuracy — simply upload a bare-face selfie in natural light and get your season type in 60 seconds. For the most thorough at-home assessment, compare warm vs. cool colors held near your face in natural daylight.
colorGuide.faq4Q: How much does professional color analysis cost?
colorGuide.faq4A: In-person professional color draping typically costs $150–$400 for a 1.5–3 hour session. Virtual consultations range from $50–$150. AI color analysis tools like Belle AI offer comparable results starting free, making color analysis accessible to everyone.
colorGuide.faq5A: Yes. Knowing your best colors saves money (fewer wardrobe mistakes), simplifies shopping, improves your professional image, and helps you look healthier and more vibrant. colorGuide.faq6A: The four main seasons are Spring (warm, light, clear), Summer (cool, muted, light), Autumn (warm, muted, deep), and Winter (cool, clear, deep). Each season is further divided into three sub-seasons for more precision, creating the 12-season system used by most modern color analysts.
colorGuide.faq7A: Your fundamental undertone doesn't change, but your apparent season can shift slightly with major changes like going gray, significant tanning, or aging. Most people remain in the same season family throughout life, though they may shift between sub-seasons.
colorGuide.faq8Q: What is the rarest color season?
colorGuide.faq8A: Bright Winter (Clear Winter) is the rarest of the 12 sub-seasons, representing about 5.4% of people. Soft Summer is the most common at around 13%. However, rarity varies by region and ethnicity — certain seasons are more common in specific populations.
colorGuide.faq9A: Modern AI color analysis achieves results comparable to professional consultations for most people. AI analyzes undertone, depth, contrast, and chroma from your photo using the same color science principles that professional colorists use. For best accuracy, use a clear bare-face selfie in natural daylight with no makeup or filters.
colorGuide.faq10Q: What is the difference between 4-season and 12-season color analysis?
colorGuide.faq10A: The 4-season system groups people into Spring, Summer, Autumn, or Winter. The 12-season system divides each season into three sub-types for greater precision — for example, Autumn splits into Soft Autumn, Warm Autumn, and Deep Autumn. The 12-season system is more accurate because it accounts for the nuances within each season family.

dark-skin.name: Dark Skin Tones
dark-skin.heroDesc: Dark skin tones carry incredible depth and richness that pair beautifully with both bold jewel tones and warm earthy shades. However, traditional color analysis systems were not originally designed with diverse skin tones in mind. This guide specifically addresses how color analysis works for deeper complexions and how to find your most flattering palette.
dark-skin.undertone: For dark skin tones, check undertone by comparing pure gold jewelry vs. silver jewelry against your skin. Look at the inside of your lower lip — cooler undertones appear more pink-purple, while warmer undertones appear more orange-coral. You can also check behind your ear, where sun damage is minimal.

dark-skin.ch2: Color season descriptions often default to examples of lighter complexions
dark-skin.ch3: Undertone can be harder to identify visually in deeper skin tones

dark-skin.cs2: Warm Autumn — strongly warm undertones with medium-deep depth
dark-skin.cs3: Cool Winter — distinctly cool undertones with dark coloring

dark-skin.wt3: Metallics (gold, bronze, copper) complement warm undertones beautifully
dark-skin.wt4: Avoid very muted or washed-out colors that may appear chalky against your skin
dark-skin.faq0Q: Does color analysis work for dark skin?
dark-skin.faq0A: Absolutely. Color analysis works for all skin tones. The 12-season system categorizes people based on undertone (warm vs. cool), depth (light vs. dark), and chroma (clear vs. muted) — these dimensions apply equally to every skin tone. The key is finding a method (like AI analysis) that has been calibrated for diverse complexions.
dark-skin.faq1Q: What color season are most dark-skinned people?
dark-skin.faq1A: Dark skin tones most commonly fall into Deep Winter (cool-neutral undertones) or Deep Autumn (warm undertones). However, all 12 seasons are possible — it depends on your specific combination of undertone, contrast, and chroma, not just depth.
dark-skin.faq2Q: How do I find my undertone with dark skin?
dark-skin.faq2A: Try the gold vs. silver test — if gold jewelry looks more natural, you're likely warm-toned. Check the inside of your lower lip: pink-purple = cool, orange-coral = warm. Look at the area behind your ear for the most reliable skin color reading.

men.name: Men
men.heroDesc: Color analysis isn't just for women. Knowing your best colors can transform your professional image, simplify shopping, and ensure every suit, shirt, and casual outfit works with your natural coloring. Men who understand their color season make better wardrobe investments and always look polished.
men.undertone: For men, the easiest undertone test is comparing a white shirt to an off-white/cream shirt against your face. If bright white brightens your face, you're likely cool-toned. If cream looks better, you're likely warm-toned. Also notice whether silver or gold watch cases look more natural on your wrist.

men.ch1: Facial hair color affects contrast level, which can change your season presentation
men.ch2: Professional dress codes limit color choices, making subtle optimization crucial

men.faq0Q: Is color analysis useful for men?
men.faq0A: Very much so. Men's wardrobes rely heavily on neutrals, and knowing which neutrals (cool gray vs. warm brown, white vs. cream) flatter you most can save money and elevate your professional image. Even small color adjustments — like choosing the right blue for a suit — make a noticeable difference.
men.faq1Q: What colors should men wear to look more attractive?
men.faq1A: Research consistently shows navy, deep blue, and black as most attractive on men. However, your best specific shades depend on your color season. A Warm Autumn man looks better in warm navy and chocolate brown, while a Cool Winter man looks sharper in blue-black and cool gray.
men.faq2Q: Does facial hair affect my color season?
men.faq2A: Facial hair doesn't change your underlying season, but it can affect your apparent contrast level. A full dark beard on light skin increases contrast, potentially making your styling recommendations lean toward higher-contrast palettes within your season.

asian-skin.name: Asian Skin Tones
asian-skin.heroDesc: Asian skin tones span a wide range — from fair with cool pink undertones to deep with warm golden undertones. Personal color analysis is extremely popular in East Asia (especially Korea and Japan, where it's called パーソナルカラー and 퍼스널컬러), and for good reason: the right colors can dramatically transform how healthy and vibrant your skin looks.
asian-skin.undertone: For Asian skin, the most reliable tests are: (1) Gold vs silver jewelry comparison — hold each against your jaw; (2) Look at the skin on your inner arm in natural light — pinkish = cool, yellowish-golden = warm, olive-gray = neutral; (3) The white paper test — hold a plain white paper next to your face — if your skin looks yellowish by comparison, you're likely warm, if pinkish, you're likely cool.

asian-skin.ch1: Many people assume Asian skin is automatically warm (yellow-toned), but cool and neutral undertones are very common

asian-skin.ch3: Natural hair color (very dark brown to black) can create undertone confusion
asian-skin.ch4: Popular K-beauty and J-beauty trends may push colors that aren't universally flattering

asian-skin.faq0A: No — this is a common misconception. While many Asian skin tones have yellow melanin, undertone is about whether that yellow leans warm (golden) or cool (olive/grayish). Many East Asians are actually Cool Summer or Cool Winter. The only way to know is to test against warm and cool colors.
asian-skin.faq1Q: Why is personal color analysis so popular in Korea and Japan?
asian-skin.faq1A: In Korea (퍼스널컬러) and Japan (パーソナルカラー), personal color analysis became a mainstream beauty practice because the subtle differences between warm and cool makeup shades have a very visible impact on Asian skin tones. Professional draping salons are common, and K-beauty brands increasingly label products by season type.
asian-skin.faq2Q: What's the most common color season for Asian people?
asian-skin.faq2A: There's no single dominant season — it varies widely by individual. That said, Cool Summer and Warm Autumn are statistically common among East Asians, while South Asians frequently test as Deep Autumn or Deep Winter. AI color analysis gives the most accurate individual result.

olive-skin.name: Olive Skin Tones
olive-skin.heroDesc: Olive undertone is arguably the most misunderstood and misdiagnosed skin tone in color analysis. Olive skin has a green or grayish cast that makes it appear neither purely warm nor purely cool. This unique undertone doesn't fit neatly into traditional warm/cool categories, which is why many olive-toned people get incorrect season results from basic quizzes.
olive-skin.undertone: Olive undertone has a distinct greenish or grayish cast visible when compared to standard warm (golden) or cool (pink) tones. To identify it: (1) Both gold and silver jewelry look decent but neither looks perfect; (2) Your skin looks slightly greenish-gray next to white paper; (3) Many foundation shades look too pink or too yellow on you; (4) You may notice a greenish tint on your neck or jawline.

olive-skin.faq0Q: Is olive a warm or cool undertone?
olive-skin.faq0A: Olive is actually a neutral undertone with a green/gray cast. It can lean warm (warm olive) or cool (cool olive), but it's distinct from standard warm or cool. This is why olive-toned people often get contradictory results from simple warm/cool tests.
olive-skin.faq1Q: Why is olive skin so hard to color-type?
olive-skin.faq1A: Because the green/gray cast of olive skin doesn't fit the standard warm (golden) vs. cool (pink) framework that most color analysis systems use. Both warm and cool colors can look slightly off, and vein/jewelry tests give mixed signals. AI color analysis with photo input tends to be more accurate than quiz-based methods for olive skin.
olive-skin.faq2Q: What colors should olive skin avoid?
olive-skin.faq2A: Generally avoid very bright, saturated colors (especially neon orange, bright coral, and vivid yellow) that can make olive skin look sallow. Also be cautious with very cool pastels (icy pink, baby blue) that may clash with the green undertone. Stick to muted, earthy, and medium-depth colors.

fair-skin.name: Fair Skin Tones
fair-skin.heroDesc: Fair skin tones have unique color analysis considerations. Because there's less melanin in the skin, undertone signals can be more visible (you might see redness, blue veins, or golden warmth more clearly), but low contrast between skin and features can make season typing tricky. The right colors make fair skin look luminous; the wrong ones make it look washed out or ruddy.
fair-skin.undertone: Fair skin actually makes undertone identification easier in some ways: vein color is more visible (blue = cool, green = warm, mix = neutral). Look at your face in natural light — if you see pinkness, you're likely cool. If you see golden warmth, you're likely warm. If you sunburn easily and rarely tan, you're more likely cool-toned.

fair-skin.faq1Q: Why do some colors make my fair skin look ruddy or sallow?
fair-skin.faq1A: Colors that clash with your undertone emphasize the 'wrong' pigments in your skin. If you're cool-toned, warm colors like orange or mustard can make your skin look yellowish. If you're warm-toned, cool colors like icy pink or silver can bring out redness.

beginners.name: Beginners
beginners.heroDesc: If you've heard about color analysis on TikTok, Instagram, or from a friend and want to understand what it's all about — you're in the right place. This beginner-friendly guide breaks down everything you need to know, step by step, without jargon or assumptions about what you already know.
beginners.undertone: Start with the most basic test: hold a piece of pure white paper next to your bare face in natural light. If your skin looks slightly yellowish/golden by comparison, you likely have warm undertones. If it looks pinkish/rosy, you likely have cool undertones. If it's hard to tell, you may be neutral. This one test narrows your season possibilities from 12 to about 6.

beginners.faq0A: Color analysis (also called seasonal color analysis or personal color analysis) is a method of finding the specific colors that look best on you based on your natural coloring — skin tone, eye color, and hair color. It categorizes people into 'seasons' (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter) with sub-types for more precision, each with its own recommended color palette.
beginners.faq1Q: How do I get started with color analysis?
beginners.faq1A: The fastest way is to try a free AI color analysis — upload a bare-face selfie in natural light and get your season type in 60 seconds. You can also take a free online quiz for a quick estimate, or book a professional draping session ($200+) for the most thorough experience.
beginners.faq2A: Color analysis is based on color theory principles — specifically how different colors interact with your skin's undertone, creating either harmonious or clashing visual effects. While it's not 'hard science,' the underlying principles of color harmony and contrast are well-established in art, design, and optics.
beginners.faq3A: Your fundamental undertone doesn't change, but your apparent season can shift slightly with major changes like going gray, significant tanning, or aging. Your underlying season remains the same — what changes is how you present it. Periodic re-analysis is useful after major appearance changes.

medium-skin.name: Medium Skin Tones
medium-skin.heroDesc: Medium skin tones are the most common globally and span the widest range of undertones — from warm golden to cool pink to neutral olive. Because medium skin has moderate depth, the undertone and chroma dimensions become especially important for color typing. The right colors make medium skin look vibrant and healthy; the wrong ones can make it look sallow or washed out.
medium-skin.undertone: For medium skin tones, the jewelry test is most reliable: try on gold and silver separately and see which looks more harmonious against your skin. Also look at your inner wrist veins — blue/purple = cool, green = warm, mixed = neutral. Because medium skin can have any undertone, take your time with this step.

medium-skin.faq1Q: Why do some colors make my medium skin look sallow?

redheads.name: Redheads & Auburn Hair

Redheads have distinctive coloring that interacts with clothing and makeup colors in specific ways. redheads.undertone: Most redheads have warm undertones, but cool-toned redheads do exist (especially those with ashy strawberry hair). Check if your skin has peachy-golden warmth (warm) or pink-rosy coolness (cool). If your freckles are golden-brown, you're almost certainly warm-toned. If they're grayish, you may lean cool.

neutral-undertone.faq0Q: How do I know if I have neutral undertones?
neutral-undertone.faq0A: If you look equally good in gold and silver jewelry, your veins appear blue-green, and you can wear both warm and cool colors without looking washed out, you likely have neutral undertones.
neutral-undertone.faq1Q: Which color season is best for neutral undertones?
neutral-undertone.faq1A: Neutral undertones most commonly fall into Soft Summer (cool-leaning) or Soft Autumn (warm-leaning). AI analysis can detect the subtle lean in your undertone.
neutral-undertone.faq2Q: Can neutral undertones wear both warm and cool colors?
neutral-undertone.faq2A: Yes — that is the biggest advantage. You can pull from both warm and cool palettes, though muted and medium-saturation shades tend to be most flattering.
neutral-undertone.undertone: Neutral undertones often have a mix of both warm and cool indicators. Your veins may appear blue-green. You likely tan easily without burning but do not turn very golden. The key is identifying whether you lean slightly warm-neutral or cool-neutral.

mature-skin.name: Mature Skin (40+)
mature-skin.heroDesc: As we age, our coloring naturally evolves — hair may gray or lighten, skin may lose some depth, and contrast levels shift. These changes can mean the colors that looked amazing at 25 no longer have the same effect. Color analysis for mature skin helps you adapt your palette to your current coloring, ensuring you always look vibrant, healthy, and polished rather than washed out or overpowered.

mature-skin.ch4: Foundation matching becomes trickier as skin tone changes
mature-skin.ug: Your undertone typically stays consistent as you age, but depth and contrast often shift. As hair grays, warm types may appear cooler. Reassess your color season every few years.

mature-skin.cs1: Soft Autumn — warm undertones with softer, less contrasted features
mature-skin.cs2: Light Summer — lighter complexions with silver or white hair

mature-skin.faq0Q: Does my color season change as I age?
mature-skin.faq0A: Your undertone stays the same, but your optimal sub-season may shift as hair grays and skin loses depth. Re-analysis every few years is recommended.
mature-skin.faq1Q: What colors make mature skin look younger?
mature-skin.faq1A: Rich, saturated colors like teal, raspberry, plum, and sapphire add vibrancy near the face. Avoid washed-out pastels and heavy black.
mature-skin.faq2Q: Should I still wear black after 40?
mature-skin.faq2A: Black can create harsh contrast against aging skin. Consider softer dark neutrals like charcoal, deep navy, or espresso. If you love black, add a flattering color near your face.
mature-skin.undertone: Your undertone typically stays consistent as you age, but depth and contrast often shift. As hair grays, warm types may appear cooler. Reassess your color season every few years.

curly-hair.faq0Q: Does curly hair affect my color season?
curly-hair.faq0A: Your hair texture does not change your color season, but it affects how hair color appears. Curly hair looks darker than straight hair at the same level.
curly-hair.faq1Q: What hair colors work best on curly hair?
curly-hair.faq1A: Colors with dimension — like balayage, highlights, or rich shades — look stunning on curls because the pattern naturally creates light play.
curly-hair.faq2Q: How do I maintain colored curly hair?
curly-hair.faq2A: Use sulfate-free, color-safe products. Deep condition regularly. Avoid excessive heat styling. Refresh color every 8-10 weeks.
curly-hair.undertone: Determine your undertone independently from hair color. Your natural curl color is a good indicator — warm-toned curls (golden, copper) suggest warm undertones, ashy or cool-brown curls suggest cool.

oval.faq1Q: What is an oval face shape?
oval.faq1A: An oval face shape is slightly longer than wide with a gently rounded jawline. The forehead is slightly wider than the jaw, and the cheekbones are the widest part. It is considered the most versatile face shape for hairstyles and glasses.
oval.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on an oval face?
oval.faq2A: Almost any hairstyle works on an oval face — long layers, classic bobs, side parts, pixie cuts, and sleek straight styles all look great. The balanced proportions mean you have maximum flexibility.
oval.faq3Q: What glasses suit an oval face?
oval.faq3A: Virtually any frame shape complements an oval face. Rectangular frames add structure, cat-eye frames add vintage elegance, and aviators create a classic look. Avoid oversized frames that overwhelm your proportions.
oval.faq4Q: How should I contour an oval face?
oval.faq4A: Light contouring under the cheekbones enhances your natural bone structure. Highlight the center of the forehead, nose bridge, and chin. Apply blush to the apples of the cheeks, blending upward.
oval.faq5Q: Which celebrities have an oval face?
oval.faq5A: Bella Hadid, Beyoncé, and Jessica Alba are well-known examples of the oval face shape.

round.faq1Q: What is a round face shape?
round.faq1A: A round face shape has width and length that are nearly equal, with full cheeks, a rounded jawline, and soft angles. It gives a youthful, friendly appearance.
round.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on a round face?
round.faq2A: Long layers, side parts, asymmetrical bobs, and styles with height at the crown help elongate a round face. Face-framing layers below the chin add definition.
round.faq3Q: What glasses suit a round face?
round.faq3A: Angular or rectangular frames add definition. Cat-eye and geometric frames create contrast with the soft curves. Avoid small, round frames that mirror the face shape.
round.faq4Q: How should I contour a round face?
round.faq4A: Contour the sides of the forehead and under the cheekbones. Apply bronzer along the jawline to slim and define. Highlight the center of the face vertically.
round.faq5Q: Which celebrities have a round face?
round.faq5A: Selena Gomez, Chrissy Teigen, and Ginnifer Goodwin are well-known examples of the round face shape.

square.faq1Q: What is a square face shape?
square.faq1A: A square face has a strong, angular jawline with the forehead, cheekbones, and jaw approximately the same width. It creates a powerful, structured appearance.
square.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on a square face?
square.faq2A: Soft waves, long layered cuts, side-swept styles, and rounded bobs soften angular features. Textured, tousled styles with movement work beautifully.
square.faq3Q: What glasses suit a square face?
square.faq3A: Round or oval frames contrast the angular jawline. Rimless frames offer a softer look. Cat-eye or butterfly frames lift the face. Avoid boxy, angular frames.
square.faq4Q: How should I contour a square face?
square.faq4A: Contour the corners of the forehead and jawline to soften angles. Apply blush in round motions. Highlight the center of the face and under the eyes.
square.faq5Q: Which celebrities have a square face?
square.faq5A: Angelina Jolie, Margot Robbie, and Keira Knightley are well-known examples of the square face shape.

heart.faq1Q: What is a heart face shape?
heart.faq1A: A heart face shape is widest at the forehead and cheekbones, tapering to a delicate, pointed chin. It often features a widow's peak hairline and high cheekbones.
heart.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on a heart face?
heart.faq2A: Chin-length bobs, side-parted waves, medium layers starting at the chin, and curtain bangs help balance the wider forehead with the narrower chin.
heart.faq3Q: What glasses suit a heart face?
heart.faq3A: Bottom-heavy frames balance the wider forehead. Round or oval frames add softness. Light-colored or rimless bottom frames work well. Avoid top-heavy frames.
heart.faq4Q: How should I contour a heart face?
heart.faq4A: Contour the sides of the forehead to narrow it. Highlight the chin and jawline to balance proportions. Apply blush below the cheekbones, sweeping downward.
heart.faq5Q: Which celebrities have a heart face?
heart.faq5A: Scarlett Johansson, Reese Witherspoon, and Taylor Swift are well-known examples of the heart face shape.

oblong.faq1Q: What is an oblong face shape?
oblong.faq1A: An oblong (rectangular) face is noticeably longer than wide, with a long, straight cheek line and forehead, cheeks, and jaw of similar width.
oblong.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on an oblong face?
oblong.faq2A: Shoulder-length cuts with side volume, waves that add width, layered bobs, and full blunt bangs help shorten the face visually and add horizontal balance.
oblong.faq3Q: What glasses suit an oblong face?
oblong.faq3A: Wide, oversized frames add horizontal balance. Round or aviator styles contrast the length. Frames with a strong top line work well. Avoid small, narrow frames.
oblong.faq4Q: How should I contour an oblong face?
oblong.faq4A: Contour the forehead along the hairline and under the chin to shorten the face. Apply blush horizontally across cheeks to add width. Highlight cheekbones outward.
oblong.faq5Q: Which celebrities have an oblong face?
oblong.faq5A: Sarah Jessica Parker, Liv Tyler, and Gisele Bündchen are well-known examples of the oblong face shape.

diamond.faq1Q: What is a diamond face shape?
diamond.faq1A: A diamond face shape has wide, high cheekbones with a narrow forehead and jawline. It creates a dramatic, angular appearance with distinct geometry.
diamond.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on a diamond face?
diamond.faq2A: Chin-length bobs, side-swept bangs, tucked-behind-ear styles, and medium layers with jaw-level volume work well to balance the prominent cheekbones.
diamond.faq3Q: What glasses suit a diamond face?
diamond.faq3A: Oval or rimless frames for balance. Cat-eye frames widen the brow area. Browline frames balance the narrow forehead. Avoid narrow or angular frames.
diamond.faq4Q: How should I contour a diamond face?
diamond.faq4A: Highlight the forehead and chin to balance narrow points. Contour under the cheekbones to soften prominence. Apply lighter foundation on the forehead to widen it.
diamond.faq5Q: Which celebrities have a diamond face?
diamond.faq5A: Rihanna, Vanessa Hudgens, and Ashley Greene are well-known examples of the diamond face shape.

triangle.faq1Q: What is a triangle face shape?
triangle.faq1A: A triangle (pear-shaped) face is widest at the jawline with a narrower forehead. It creates a stable, grounded appearance with a strong lower face.
triangle.faq2Q: What hairstyles look best on a triangle face?
triangle.faq2A: Styles with volume at the top and temples, side-swept bangs, layered styles with crown volume, and textured pixie cuts help balance the wider jaw.
triangle.faq3Q: What glasses suit a triangle face?
triangle.faq3A: Cat-eye or semi-rimless frames widen the upper face. Decorative top frames with bold brow lines and aviator styles add horizontal emphasis. Avoid bottom-heavy frames.
triangle.faq4Q: How should I contour a triangle face?
triangle.faq4A: Highlight the forehead, temples, and under-eye area to widen the upper face. Contour along the jawline and under the chin to minimize width.
triangle.faq5Q: Which celebrities have a triangle face?
triangle.faq5A: Kelly Osbourne, Minnie Driver, and Jennifer Aniston are well-known examples of the triangle face shape.

spring.faq2Q: What are the three Spring sub-seasons?

summer.faq2Q: What are the three Summer sub-seasons?

summer.faq3Q: How do I know if I am a Summer?
summer.faq3A: Summers typically have cool or neutral undertones, ash-toned hair, and look best in soft, muted colors. AI analysis can identify your exact sub-season.
summer.faq4A: Summers should generally avoid warm, saturated, or very dark colors like orange, bright yellow, black, and warm earth tones.

autumn.heroDesc: Autumn color types share warm, earthy undertones with rich depth. If you shine in rust, olive, and burnt orange, you likely belong to one of the three Autumn sub-seasons.
autumn.faq1Q: What is an Autumn color type?
autumn.faq1A: An Autumn color type has warm, earthy undertones with rich, muted coloring. Autumns look best in warm earth tones like rust, olive, gold, and rich browns.
autumn.faq2Q: What are the three Autumn sub-seasons?
autumn.faq2A: Soft Autumn (blended warm-cool, muted), Warm Autumn (golden, saturated warmth), and Deep Autumn (dark, rich warmth).
autumn.faq3Q: How do I know if I am an Autumn?
autumn.faq3A: Autumns typically have warm undertones, auburn or brown hair, golden-flecked eyes, and look best in rich, earthy colors. AI analysis can confirm your sub-season.
autumn.faq4A: Autumns should generally avoid cool, bright, or icy colors like fuchsia, baby blue, silver-gray, and pure white.

winter.heroDesc: Winter color types share cool, blue or pink undertones with high contrast. If you look striking in black, white, and jewel tones, you likely belong to one of the three Winter sub-seasons.
winter.faq1Q: What is a Winter color type?
winter.faq1A: A Winter color type has cool undertones with high contrast between skin, hair, and eyes. Winters look best in bold, clear colors like true red, royal blue, emerald, and stark white.
winter.faq2Q: What are the three Winter sub-seasons?
winter.faq2A: Deep Winter (dark, cool intensity), Cool Winter (true cool with high contrast), and Bright Winter (vivid, clear colors with warm-cool balance).
winter.faq3Q: How do I know if I am a Winter?
winter.faq3A: Winters typically have cool undertones, dark hair, high contrast features, and look striking in bold, jewel-tone colors. AI analysis can determine your exact sub-season.
winter.faq4A: Winters should generally avoid warm, muted, or earthy colors like camel, olive, warm beige, and soft pastels that can wash out their high-contrast coloring.

taylor-swift.faq1Q: What is Taylor Swift's color season?
taylor-swift.faq1A: Taylor Swift is a Light Summer in the 12-season color analysis system. She has fair, cool-toned skin with low-to-medium contrast between her skin, hair, and eyes. Light Summers look best in soft, cool pastels and muted tones.
taylor-swift.faq2Q: What are Taylor Swift's best colors?
taylor-swift.faq2A: Taylor Swift's signature colors include soft lavender, dusty rose, powder blue, and soft white. These cool, muted shades complement her delicate features and appear throughout her Eras Tour wardrobe and red carpet looks.
taylor-swift.faq3Q: How does Taylor Swift use color in her style?
taylor-swift.faq3A: Taylor consistently chooses soft cool pastels on stage, avoids harsh black near her face, and uses silver metallics. Her makeup stays in the cool pink and mauve family, creating a cohesive Light Summer aesthetic across every era.

beyonce.faq1A: Beyoncé is a Warm Autumn with rich, golden-brown skin and warm undertones. Warm Autumns have medium-to-deep coloring that thrives in earthy, warm, and muted shades like terracotta, olive, and warm gold.
beyonce.faq2A: Beyoncé's best colors include terracotta, olive green, warm gold, and deep teal. She frequently wears gold metallics and earth tones that amplify her natural warmth on stage and at events.
beyonce.faq3Q: How does Beyoncé use color in her style?
beyonce.faq3A: Beyoncé masterfully uses warm bronzes, copper highlights, and rich berry lips in her makeup. She avoids icy pastels and gravitates toward gold gowns, earth-toned ensembles, and warm jewel tones that enhance her Warm Autumn radiance.

rihanna.faq1A: Rihanna is a Deep Winter with deep, cool-toned skin and high contrast features. Deep Winters look stunning in bold, saturated jewel tones and stark contrasts that would overwhelm lighter color types.
rihanna.faq2A: Rihanna's signature colors include true red, royal blue, emerald green, and pure white. She fearlessly wears bold jewel tones and high-contrast combinations that showcase the dramatic power of Deep Winter coloring.
rihanna.faq3Q: How does Rihanna use color in her style?
rihanna.faq3A: Rihanna embraces deep berry lips, smoky eyes, and cool-toned highlighters in her beauty looks. Her Fenty Beauty line reflects her understanding of deep, cool-toned complexions, and her fashion choices consistently push bold color boundaries.

zendaya.faq1A: Zendaya is a Deep Autumn with warm, deep skin and rich natural contrast. Deep Autumns have warm but intense coloring that looks best in deep, saturated earth tones and warm jewel shades.
zendaya.faq2A: Zendaya's best colors include burgundy, forest green, burnt orange, and deep teal. These deep, warm tones define her most iconic red carpet moments and complement her striking, grounded presence.
zendaya.faq3Q: How does Zendaya use color in her style?
zendaya.faq3A: Zendaya favors warm berry lips, bronze eyes, and rich contouring. She uses metallic bronze and copper accents and avoids pale pastels, consistently choosing colors with depth and warmth that match her Deep Autumn coloring.

jennie.faq1A: Jennie Kim of BLACKPINK is a Cool Winter with fair, cool-toned skin and high contrast features. Cool Winters look best in clear, cool, and bold shades with crisp, sophisticated energy.
jennie.faq2A: Jennie's signature colors include hot pink, true black, icy blue, and pure white. Monochrome black-and-white outfits and bold fuchsia accents are staples of her high-fashion aesthetic.
jennie.faq3Q: How does Jennie use color in her style?
jennie.faq3A: Jennie embraces K-fashion minimalism with sharp silhouettes and cool-toned makeup featuring pink blush and berry lips. Her chic style perfectly aligns with the Cool Winter palette's bold, high-contrast sophistication.

lisa.faq1A: Lisa of BLACKPINK is a Warm Spring with golden-tan skin and a bright, clear warmth to her overall appearance. Warm Springs shine in vivid, warm, and clear colors with lively, sunny energy.
lisa.faq2A: Lisa's best colors include coral, golden yellow, warm turquoise, and bright orange. These vivid warm brights dominate her stage costumes and street style, reflecting her energetic personality.
lisa.faq3Q: How does Lisa use color in her style?

rose.faq1A: Rosé of BLACKPINK is a Light Spring with fair, warm-toned skin and soft golden-blonde hair. Light Springs have delicate, warm luminosity that looks best in light, warm, and clear colors.
rose.faq2A: Rosé's signature colors include peach, warm pink, light coral, and buttercup yellow. These soft, warm pastels appear throughout her wardrobe and stage costumes, enhancing her ethereal aesthetic.
rose.faq3Q: How does Rosé use color in her style?
rose.faq3A: Rosé favors light, airy fabrics in warm pastels with fresh, warm makeup — peach blush, coral lips, and golden shimmer. She avoids heavy dark colors near her face that could overpower her delicate Light Spring features.

jisoo.faq1A: Jisoo of BLACKPINK is a Cool Summer with fair, cool-toned skin and muted contrast. Cool Summers look most elegant in soft, cool, and muted shades with gentle, sophisticated tones.
jisoo.faq2A: Jisoo's best colors include dusty rose, soft mauve, muted blue, and soft gray. These soft, muted cool tones define her elegant, classic style on and off stage.
jisoo.faq3Q: How does Jisoo use color in her style?
jisoo.faq3A: Jisoo chooses classic, structured pieces in cool neutrals with soft pink blush and rose lips. She avoids bright warm oranges and harsh blacks, maintaining the refined Cool Summer harmony that complements her natural coloring.

margot-robbie.faq3Q: How does Margot Robbie use color in her style?

emma-stone.faq2Q: What are Emma Stone's best colors?
emma-stone.faq2A: Emma Stone's best colors include deep teal, rust, olive, and warm ivory. Deep teal and emerald green create stunning contrast with her auburn hair, while earthy rust and olive complement her Warm Autumn warmth.
emma-stone.faq3Q: How does Emma Stone use color in her style?
emma-stone.faq3A: Emma's auburn hair is a perfect Warm Autumn choice — rich, warm, and naturally harmonious. Her makeup features warm peach blush, terracotta lips, and bronze eyeshadow that enhance her golden undertones.

lupita-nyongo.faq2Q: What are Lupita Nyong'o's best colors?

lupita-nyongo.faq3Q: How does Lupita Nyong'o use color in her style?
lupita-nyongo.faq3A: Lupita uses high-contrast color blocking on red carpets with rich berry lips and bold eye colors. She avoids muted, dusty tones and proves that Deep Winters can pull off virtually any vivid, saturated color.

timothee-chalamet.faq2Q: What are Timothée Chalamet's best colors?

timothee-chalamet.faq3Q: How does Timothée Chalamet use color in his style?

harry-styles.faq2Q: What are Harry Styles' best colors?

harry-styles.faq3Q: How does Harry Styles use color in his style?

v-bts.faq1A: V (Kim Taehyung) of BTS is a Bright Winter with fair skin, striking features, and high contrast with a touch of warmth. Bright Winters excel in vivid, clear, and bold colors.
v-bts.faq2A: V's best colors include true red, bright cobalt, pure white, and hot pink. Bold, clear colors with clean lines are staples in his fashion-forward style.
v-bts.faq3Q: How does V use color in his style?

aishwarya-rai.faq2Q: What are Aishwarya Rai's best colors?

aishwarya-rai.faq3Q: How does Aishwarya Rai use color in her style?

priyanka-chopra.faq2Q: What are Priyanka Chopra's best colors?

soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq1Q: What is the main difference between Soft Autumn and Soft Summer?
soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq1A: The main difference is undertone. Soft Autumn has warm-neutral undertones with golden, peachy warmth, while Soft Summer has cool-neutral undertones with pink or rosy coolness. Both are muted and low-contrast, which makes them the most commonly confused pair in color analysis.
soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq2Q: Can Soft Autumn wear Soft Summer colors?
soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq2A: Some overlap exists in muted tones, but Soft Autumn should prioritize warm muted shades like camel, warm taupe, and dusty coral. Soft Summer's cool dusty rose, mushroom gray, and soft mauve will make Soft Autumn skin look dull or sallow.
soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq3Q: How do I test whether I am Soft Autumn or Soft Summer?
soft-autumn-vs-soft-summer.faq3A: Hold warm gold and cool silver fabric near your bare face in natural light. If gold makes your skin glow and silver looks flat, you are Soft Autumn. If silver brightens your complexion and gold looks yellowish, you are Soft Summer.

light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq1Q: How do Light Spring and Light Summer differ?
light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq1A: Both are light and low-contrast, but Light Spring has warm golden undertones while Light Summer has cool pink or rosy undertones. Light Spring looks best in warm pastels like peach and coral; Light Summer in cool pastels like powder blue and soft lavender.
light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq2Q: I have fair skin and light hair — am I Light Spring or Light Summer?
light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq2A: Check your undertone, not just your depth. If you tan golden and look fresh in peach and warm pink, you are likely Light Spring. If you burn easily, have pink undertones, and glow in cool pastels, you are likely Light Summer.
light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq3Q: Which colors should I avoid if I am between Light Spring and Light Summer?
light-spring-vs-light-summer.faq3A: Avoid colors that are clearly wrong for both — harsh black, dark navy, and heavy burgundy overwhelm both types. Instead, test warm ivory vs soft white near your face, and peach vs powder blue to determine your undertone direction.

warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq1Q: What separates Warm Spring from Warm Autumn?
warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq1A: Both are strongly warm, but Warm Spring is clear, bright, and medium in depth with high chroma, while Warm Autumn is richer, deeper, and more muted. Think sunny vibrancy (Warm Spring) versus earthy richness (Warm Autumn).
warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq2Q: Do Warm Spring and Warm Autumn share any colors?
warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq2A: Yes — warm teal, coral, and golden tones work for both. But Warm Spring needs clearer, brighter versions while Warm Autumn prefers deeper, earthier versions like rust instead of bright orange, and mustard instead of golden yellow.
warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq3Q: How does contrast help distinguish Warm Spring from Warm Autumn?
warm-spring-vs-warm-autumn.faq3A: Warm Spring has medium contrast with a clear, lively brightness. Warm Autumn has medium contrast with a rich, grounded warmth. If vivid warm brights energize you, lean Warm Spring. If earthy, muted warm tones feel more natural, lean Warm Autumn.

bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq1Q: Why are Bright Spring and Bright Winter so often confused?
bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq1A: Both are the highest-chroma types with vivid, clear coloring and high contrast. The key difference is undertone: Bright Spring is warm-neutral and tolerates warm-leaning brights, while Bright Winter is cool-neutral and needs icy, cool clarity.
bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq2Q: Can Bright Spring wear Bright Winter colors?
bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq2A: Some overlap exists in vivid colors, but Bright Spring should favor warm coral, tangerine, and warm red. Bright Winter's hot pink, electric blue, and cool true red will look slightly off on Bright Spring's warm undertones.
bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq3Q: What is the fastest way to tell Bright Spring from Bright Winter?
bright-spring-vs-bright-winter.faq3A: Test gold vs silver jewelry and warm coral vs hot pink near your face. Bright Spring glows with gold and warm coral; Bright Winter glows with silver and hot pink. Your eye color also helps — golden warmth suggests Bright Spring, cool jewel tones suggest Bright Winter.

cool-summer-vs-cool-winter.faq1Q: How do Cool Summer and Cool Winter differ?
cool-summer-vs-cool-winter.faq1A: Both are distinctly cool, but Cool Summer is medium-depth with moderate contrast and slightly muted coloring, while Cool Winter is bold, high-contrast, and fully saturated. Cool Summer is elegant and soft; Cool Winter is striking and crisp.
cool-summer-vs-cool-winter.faq2A: Pure black can be harsh on Cool Summer, especially near the face. Cool Summer looks better in soft navy, cool gray, and cool cocoa. Cool Winter, by contrast, owns true black and pure white as signature neutrals.
cool-summer-vs-cool-winter.faq3Q: I am a cool-toned brunette — which season am I?
cool-summer-vs-cool-winter.faq3A: If medium-depth cool colors like dusty blue, teal, and soft berry look best on you, you are likely Cool Summer. If bold, saturated cool colors like true black, hot pink, and icy lavender look striking, you are likely Cool Winter.

deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq1Q: What is the main difference between Deep Autumn and Deep Winter?
deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq1A: Both are deep and high-contrast, but Deep Autumn is warm-neutral with golden warmth in the skin, while Deep Winter is cool-neutral with no warmth. Deep Autumn glows in warm dark tones like deep rust and warm olive; Deep Winter in cool dark tones like true black and deep red.
deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq2Q: Can Deep Autumn and Deep Winter share dark colors?
deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq2A: Both can wear dark, rich colors, but the undertone matters. Deep Autumn's dark colors have warmth — deep rust, dark teal, warm black. Deep Winter's dark colors are cool — true black, deep burgundy, dark navy. The wrong undertone will make skin look dull.
deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq3Q: How do I test Deep Autumn vs Deep Winter?
deep-autumn-vs-deep-winter.faq3A: Hold deep rust (warm) and true black (cool) near your face. If deep rust makes your skin glow with warmth, you are Deep Autumn. If true black makes your features pop with crisp contrast, you are Deep Winter. Gold vs silver jewelry gives the same clue.

soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq1Q: How are Soft Autumn and Warm Autumn different?
soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq1A: Both are warm Autumns, but Soft Autumn is muted and low-contrast with gentle, sun-faded warmth, while Warm Autumn is richer, more saturated, and medium-deep with strong golden-bronze warmth. Soft Autumn is subtle; Warm Autumn is rich.
soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq2Q: Can Soft Autumn wear Warm Autumn colors?
soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq2A: Vivid warm colors like burnt orange, rust, and mustard will overwhelm Soft Autumn's muted coloring. Soft Autumn should stick to dusty coral, warm taupe, camel, and sage. Warm Autumn can handle the richer, more saturated warm tones.
soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq3Q: Which Autumn type am I if I look good in earth tones?
soft-autumn-vs-warm-autumn.faq3A: If muted earth tones like warm taupe and sage look best, you are Soft Autumn. If rich earth tones like terracotta, rust, and mustard energize you, you are Warm Autumn. Test a dusty coral (Soft Autumn) vs burnt orange (Warm Autumn) to confirm.

light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq1Q: What distinguishes Light Spring from Bright Spring?
light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq1A: Both are warm Springs, but Light Spring is light, delicate, and low-contrast, while Bright Spring is vivid, clear, and high-contrast. Light Spring needs soft warm pastels; Bright Spring needs saturated, clear warm brights.
light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq2Q: Can a fair-skinned person be Bright Spring?
light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq2A: Yes — Bright Spring is about clarity and contrast, not depth. A fair-skinned person with striking, jewel-like eyes and high contrast between features can be Bright Spring. If dark colors near the face don't overwhelm you and vivid colors energize you, consider Bright Spring.
light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq3Q: How do I test Light Spring vs Bright Spring?
light-spring-vs-bright-spring.faq3A: Try buttercup yellow (Light Spring) vs bright yellow or hot coral (Bright Spring). If soft, light warm tones look best, you are Light Spring. If vivid, clear warm brights look amazing and dark colors don't overwhelm you, you are Bright Spring.

cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq1Q: What is the difference between Cool Summer and Soft Summer?
cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq1A: Both are cool-leaning Summers, but Cool Summer is a true cool type with medium chroma and moderate contrast, while Soft Summer is the most muted Summer with the lowest contrast. Cool Summer is clearer; Soft Summer is dustier and more blended.
cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq2Q: Is Soft Summer the same as Cool Summer?
cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq2A: No. Soft Summer is the most muted of all 12 seasons with very low chroma, while Cool Summer has medium chroma and can wear clearer cool colors like teal, steel blue, and raspberry. Soft Summer needs everything in dusty, muted versions.
cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq3Q: How do I know if I am Cool Summer or Soft Summer?
cool-summer-vs-soft-summer.faq3A: If medium-depth cool colors like teal and berry look great on you, you are likely Cool Summer. If only the dustiest, most muted cool tones work and vivid colors of any kind overwhelm you, you are likely Soft Summer.

deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq1Q: How do Deep Autumn and Soft Autumn compare?
deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq1A: Both are warm Autumns, but Deep Autumn is dark, rich, and high-contrast, while Soft Autumn is muted, gentle, and low-contrast. Deep Autumn has dramatic intensity; Soft Autumn has sun-faded softness.
deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq2Q: Can Soft Autumn wear Deep Autumn colors?
deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq2A: Dark, saturated colors like dark chocolate and deep rust will overpower Soft Autumn's gentle coloring. Soft Autumn should stay in camel, warm taupe, and dusty coral. Deep Autumn needs the depth and richness that Soft Autumn cannot handle.
deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq3Q: I have warm undertones and medium coloring — which Autumn am I?
deep-autumn-vs-soft-autumn.faq3A: If you have dark hair, intense eyes, and high contrast, test Deep Autumn colors like dark chocolate and deep rust. If your features blend softly with muted warmth, test Soft Autumn colors like camel and sage. Near-black feeling powerful suggests Deep Autumn.

deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq1Q: What separates Deep Winter from Cool Winter?
deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq1A: Both are cool Winters with high contrast, but Deep Winter is the darkest type with very deep overall coloring, while Cool Winter is the true cool type at medium-deep depth. Deep Winter needs the darkest colors; Cool Winter excels at crisp black-and-white contrast.
deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq2Q: Can Cool Winter wear Deep Winter colors?
deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq2A: Cool Winter can wear many Deep Winter colors like black, deep red, and forest green. However, Cool Winter also shines in icy pastels and pure white combinations that Deep Winter may find too light. Cool Winter has slightly more range at the lighter end.
deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq3Q: How do I test Deep Winter vs Cool Winter?
deep-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq3A: If only the deepest jewel tones work and your overall coloring is very dark and intense, lean Deep Winter. If icy pastels and black-and-white combinations look striking alongside deep cool colors, lean Cool Winter.

bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq1Q: How are Bright Winter and Cool Winter different?
bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq1A: Both are cool Winters, but Bright Winter has the highest chroma and contrast of any type — vivid, electric colors are essential. Cool Winter is bold and cool but doesn't need neon-level brights. Bright Winter is the most vivid; Cool Winter is the purest cool.
bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq2Q: Is Bright Winter rarer than Cool Winter?
bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq2A: Yes. Bright Winter represents only about 5% of people and is the rarest 12-season type. Cool Winter is more common among cool-toned individuals with dark hair and high contrast features.
bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq3Q: How do I tell Bright Winter from Cool Winter?
bright-winter-vs-cool-winter.faq3A: If hot pink, lime green, and electric blue look amazing on you — not just good, but spectacular — you are likely Bright Winter. If royal blue, true red, and fuchsia look bold and striking but you don't need neon-level intensity, you are likely Cool Winter.

warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq1Q: What is the difference between Warm Spring and Light Spring?
warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq1A: Both are warm Springs, but Warm Spring is the true, saturated Spring with medium depth and contrast, while Light Spring is the lightest and most delicate Spring with low contrast. Warm Spring is vibrant; Light Spring is luminous.
warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq2Q: Can Light Spring wear Warm Spring colors?
warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq2A: Saturated warm brights like tangerine and grass green will overwhelm Light Spring's delicate coloring. Light Spring should stay in peach, warm pink, buttercup yellow, and light coral. Warm Spring can handle the full saturation.
warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq3Q: How do I test Warm Spring vs Light Spring?
warm-spring-vs-light-spring.faq3A: Try tangerine (Warm Spring) vs peach (Light Spring). If vivid warm brights energize you and medium contrast feels natural, you are Warm Spring. If soft, light warm tones look best and dark colors overwhelm you, you are Light Spring.

warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq1Q: How do Warm Autumn and Deep Autumn differ?
warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq1A: Both are warm Autumns, but Warm Autumn is the true Autumn with medium-deep richness and moderate saturation, while Deep Autumn adds Winter depth with dark, intense coloring and high contrast. Warm Autumn is earthy-rich; Deep Autumn is dark-dramatic.
warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq2Q: Can Warm Autumn wear Deep Autumn colors?
warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq2A: Warm Autumn can wear some Deep Autumn colors like deep teal and warm burgundy, but the darkest tones like dark chocolate and warm black may be too intense. Warm Autumn looks best in terracotta, rust, mustard, and warm olive.
warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq3Q: I have warm dark hair — am I Warm Autumn or Deep Autumn?
warm-autumn-vs-deep-autumn.faq3A: If near-black and dark chocolate feel natural and create dramatic contrast, lean Deep Autumn. If warm brown, camel, and terracotta feel more harmonious and your contrast is moderate, lean Warm Autumn.

light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq1Q: What distinguishes Light Summer from Cool Summer?
light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq1A: Both are cool Summers, but Light Summer is the lightest and most delicate with very low contrast, while Cool Summer is the true Summer at medium depth with moderate contrast. Light Summer needs the lightest cool pastels; Cool Summer wears medium-depth cool tones.
light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq2Q: Can Light Summer wear Cool Summer colors?
light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq2A: Medium-depth Cool Summer colors like teal, steel blue, and soft navy may be too deep for Light Summer's delicate coloring. Light Summer should stay in powder blue, soft lavender, rose pink, and soft white.
light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq3Q: How do I test Light Summer vs Cool Summer?
light-summer-vs-cool-summer.faq3A: Try powder blue (Light Summer) vs steel blue (Cool Summer). If the lightest cool pastels look perfect and dark colors overwhelm you, you are Light Summer. If medium-depth cool tones like teal and berry look elegant, you are Cool Summer.
